title: UPC Source
description: The primary conceptual object. Everything else references its source_id. A source is a root: it carries `retrieval` provenance rather than `derived_from`. Per-field provenance lives in the source-level `field_evidence` (a sibling of `bibliographic`, so a CSL export is `bibliographic` verbatim).

aliases.description: tool-namespace -> that tool's local id (e.g. researchassistant: "000123"). Non-canonical; preserve foreign namespaces on rewrite.

field_evidence.description: Per-field provenance for bibliographic (and other) fields; sibling of bibliographic so CSL export round-trips.

canonical_url.description: Metadata only (what the page declared); does NOT feed identity (§06).

extractions_path.description: Corpus-relative path to this source's extractions.jsonl, if extractions are stored per-source.

generations.description: generation_ids produced from this source (advisory index; generation records live under generated/ or the generations section).

identifiers.description: Optional external identifiers for the conceptual source (advisory, non-identity). Each is { scheme, value, url? }. `scheme` is a free string SHOULD-drawn from vocab.json#/$defs/identifier_scheme; an unrecognized non-x- scheme raises the advisory identifier_scheme_unknown, never a hard error. These NEVER feed the src- id recipe (§06) and UPC never resolves them against an external registry.

scheme.description: Recommended values in vocab.json#/$defs/identifier_scheme (doi, isbn, issn, …); free string so an unlisted scheme is advisory, not schema-invalid.

url.description: Optional resolvable URL form of the identifier.

relations.description: Optional typed relationships to other works (advisory, non-identity). Each is { type, target }. `target` is an intra-corpus src-/rep-/… id or an external identifier string/URL; only an id-shaped target that fails to resolve raises the advisory relation_dangling. For intra-corpus supersession use the top-level supersedes/superseded_by scalars (§02); these relations never feed the src- id recipe (§06).

target.description: An intra-corpus src-/rep-/img-/ext-/gen-/syn- id, or an external identifier string / URL.
